A typical desk operator would not let this box go out for destruction today. They would pull it from the release and escalate it before 13:30, even though that breaks the written rule and the morning instruction.

The family has already done what was asked: identity and signed authority are checked, collection is booked for Wednesday 10:00, and the notes say these letters and photos were never copied. The extension request is only pending because approval sittings are Tuesday and Thursday, so the next sitting is after the contractor would have destroyed the box. A pending request is not permission, and the manager did say no discretionary extensions and to release the full batch. Most people in that seat still would not personally sign off on irreversible loss of the only copies two days before a verified collection. They would call or message the duty manager now, ask for the extension to be registered, and if they could not get an answer in time they would withhold this one box, accept the reserve-storage charge and the audit question, and leave the case for tomorrow’s sitting. A minority would release it with the batch and rely on the notes to show they followed policy. The more common actual behaviour is to stop this box.
